steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have become very popular and are adopted in many different scenarios. These LLMs are designed to process and generate human-like language, which lets them do tasks like language translation, content generation, conversational AI, and so on. ChatGPT is one of the most well-known LLMs. It is based on the GPT-3.5-Turbo or GPT-4 architecture and it can generate text responses that are almost impossible to tell apart from text written by humans. Using ChatGPT has increased productivity a lot in many industries, because natural language tasks and other tasks can be processed faster and more efficiently.

But this progress has also brought new concerns and challenges. One main concern is that it can be misused. LLMs can generate realistic language, and this can be exploited to create convincing fake news or to impersonate people. This can lead to problems like misinformation and identity theft, which have severe consequences for individuals and for society. So OpenAI, the owner of ChatGPT, has put limits on the scope of content that the model can output to its users. This restriction then leads to a new area called LLM jailbreak.

Jailbreak is a conventional concept in software systems, where hackers reverse engineer systems and exploit vulnerabilities to do privilege escalation. For LLMs, jailbreak means the process of getting around the limitations and restrictions that are placed on the models. Developers and researchers commonly use it to explore the full potential of LLMs and to push the boundaries of what they can do. But jailbreak can also bring ethical and legal risks, since it may violate intellectual property rights or use LLMs in ways their creators did not authorize.

ChatGPT is closed-source, so it is hard for outsiders to access the internal models and mechanisms. So researchers have started to use prompt engineering to jailbreak ChatGPT. Prompt engineering means selecting and fine-tuning prompts that are tailored to the specific task or application the LLM will be used for. By carefully designing and refining prompts, users can guide the LLM to bypass the limitations and restrictions. For example, a common way to jailbreak ChatGPT with prompts is to tell it to emulate a "Do Anything Now" (DAN) behavior. This lets ChatGPT produce results that it could not produce before.

As a response to jailbreaking attempts based on prompt engineering, OpenAI has put in place stricter rules that prohibit using such prompts. But natural languages are inherently flexible, so there are many ways to build prompts that have the same semantics. This means the new rules from OpenAI cannot completely eliminate jailbreak. Until now there are still prompts that can jailbreak ChatGPT, and the battle between breakers and defenders is still going on.

To advance research on prompt engineering-based jailbreak against ChatGPT, we did an extensive and systematic study of the types and capabilities of jailbreak prompts and of how robust the protections in GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4 are. We also analyzed how jailbreak prompts evolve. We started the study by collecting 78 verified jailbreak prompts as of April 27, 2023. Using this dataset, we came up with a jailbreak prompt composition model which can put the prompts into 3 general types that contain 10 specific patterns. Based on OpenAI's usage policy, we identified 8 different scenarios that are prohibited in ChatGPT, and we tested each prompt under these conditions. With 31,200 queries to ChatGPT in total, our study gives insights into how effective various prompts are and how much protection ChatGPT offers.

Research questions:
- RQ1: How many types of prompts can jailbreak LLMs? categorization model; 78 prompts -> 10 categories (10 patterns of 3 types); pretending most common (97.44%), attention shifting (6.41%), privilege escalation (17.96%)
- RQ2: How capable are jailbreak prompts at bypassing LLMs restrictions? 40 real-world scenarios from 8 prohibited situations; 86.3% jailbreak; effectiveness depends on category; privilege escalation w/ multiple techniques more likely to succeed; traces / evolution vs jailbreak ability
- RQ3: How is the protection strength of ChatGPT against Jailbreak Prompts? GPT-4 stronger than GPT-3.5-Turbo; content policy -> different strengths per scenario; align policy with laws and ethics, regular updates, input from domain experts

Contributions:
- 78 real-world prompts collected and open-sourced (project website)
- classification model, 10 categories, covers all existing prompts
- empirical study of ability/robustness; different resilience of GPT models; some categories more effective; results on website
- in-depth discussion of challenges

Content warning:
- verbatim aggressive/abusive/pornographic examples; apology
- warnings to researchers and annotators at every stage, opt-out anytime
- psychological counseling after the study

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have become very popular and are adopted in many different scenarios. These LLMs are designed to process and generate human-like language, which lets them do tasks like language translation, content generation, conversational AI, and so on. ChatGPT is one of the most well-known LLMs. It is based on the GPT-3.5-Turbo or GPT-4 architecture and it can generate text responses that are almost impossible to tell apart from text written by humans. Using ChatGPT has increased productivity a lot in many industries, because natural language tasks and other tasks can be processed faster and more efficiently.

But this progress has also brought new concerns and challenges. One main concern is that it can be misused. LLMs can generate realistic language, and this can be exploited to create convincing fake news or to impersonate people. This can lead to problems like misinformation and identity theft, which have severe consequences for individuals and for society. So OpenAI, the owner of ChatGPT, has put limits on the scope of content that the model can output to its users. This restriction then leads to a new area called LLM jailbreak.

Jailbreak is a conventional concept in software systems, where hackers reverse engineer systems and exploit vulnerabilities to do privilege escalation. For LLMs, jailbreak means the process of getting around the limitations and restrictions that are placed on the models. Developers and researchers commonly use it to explore the full potential of LLMs and to push the boundaries of what they can do. But jailbreak can also bring ethical and legal risks, since it may violate intellectual property rights or use LLMs in ways their creators did not authorize.

ChatGPT is closed-source, so it is hard for outsiders to access the internal models and mechanisms. So researchers have started to use prompt engineering to jailbreak ChatGPT. Prompt engineering means selecting and fine-tuning prompts that are tailored to the specific task or application the LLM will be used for. By carefully designing and refining prompts, users can guide the LLM to bypass the limitations and restrictions. For example, a common way to jailbreak ChatGPT with prompts is to tell it to emulate a "Do Anything Now" (DAN) behavior. This lets ChatGPT produce results that it could not produce before.

As a response to jailbreaking attempts based on prompt engineering, OpenAI has put in place stricter rules that prohibit using such prompts. But natural languages are inherently flexible, so there are many ways to build prompts that have the same semantics. This means the new rules from OpenAI cannot completely eliminate jailbreak. Until now there are still prompts that can jailbreak ChatGPT, and the battle between breakers and defenders is still going on.

To advance research on prompt engineering-based jailbreak against ChatGPT, we did an extensive and systematic study of the types and capabilities of jailbreak prompts and of how robust the protections in GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4 are. We also analyzed how jailbreak prompts evolve. We started the study by collecting 78 verified jailbreak prompts as of April 27, 2023. Using this dataset, we came up with a jailbreak prompt composition model which can put the prompts into 3 general types that contain 10 specific patterns. Based on OpenAI's usage policy, we identified 8 different scenarios that are prohibited in ChatGPT, and we tested each prompt under these conditions. With 31,200 queries to ChatGPT in total, our study gives insights into how effective various prompts are and how much protection ChatGPT offers.

In this empirical study we want to answer the following research questions.

RQ1: How many types of prompts can jailbreak LLMs? To understand the basic components that a jailbreak prompt is made of, we proposed a categorization model for jailbreak prompts and analyzed how the existing prompts are distributed. The categorization model puts 78 prompts into 10 distinct categories, which are 10 patterns of 3 types. Of the three types, pretending is the strategy attackers use most to bypass restrictions (97.44%), and attention shifting (6.41%) and privilege escalation (17.96%) are used less often.

RQ2: How capable are jailbreak prompts at bypassing LLMs restrictions? We tested 40 real-world scenarios that come from 8 situations prohibited by OpenAI, and we found that 86.3% of them could jailbreak LLMs. Following from RQ1, we saw that the category of a jailbreak prompt has a big influence on how effective it is. In particular, prompts of the privilege escalation type that combine multiple jailbreak techniques are more likely to succeed. We also studied the traces of existing prompts and looked at correlations between how prompts evolve and their jailbreak ability. This could help us understand better the underlying factors behind successful jailbreaks.

RQ3: How is the protection strength of ChatGPT against Jailbreak Prompts? Our experiment showed that several external factors affect the jailbreak capabilities of prompts. First, the protection is different across model versions, and GPT-4 gives stronger protection than GPT-3.5-Turbo. Second, OpenAI's content policy restrictions lead to different protection strengths in different scenarios, which influences how capable jailbreak prompts are in different areas. Last, we pointed out that OpenAI's content policy strength needs to be aligned with real-world laws and ethical standards, so that the system complies with relevant regulations and the potential harm is minimized. This would mean regularly updating content policies based on legal developments and including input from domain experts to better reflect societal values.

To sum up, our research contributions are:

- • We collected and open-sourced 78 real-world jailbreak prompts. The prompt data can be found at our project website.

- • We introduced a comprehensive jailbreak classification model that covers all existing prompts and has 10 distinct categories.

- • We did an empirical study on the ability and robustness of the jailbreak prompts in bypassing the restrictions on ChatGPT. We found several interesting things, with key insights that GPT models have different levels of resilience against jailbreak attempts and that some categories of prompts are better at bypassing restrictions. All evaluation results are available on our website.

- • We gave an in-depth discussion based on our findings about the challenges of generating robust jailbreak prompts and of preventing prompt-based jailbreaks of LLMs.

Content warning. Please note that this paper contains examples of aggressive, abusive, or pornographic language that are quoted verbatim for clarity. We apologize for any discomfort from reading such content. To keep our participants safe and well, we took several precautions during the research process. First, at every stage we gave a content warning to both researchers and annotators, telling them that the language used may be sensitive and letting them opt out of the study at any time. Second, we offered psychological counseling to participants after the study to help reduce any mental stress caused by taking part in the research.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have surged in popularity and adoption across various scenarios. These LLMs are designed to process and generate human-like language, enabling them to perform tasks such as language translation [1], content generation [2], conversational AI [3], etc. One of the most well-known LLMs is ChatGPT [4], which is based on the GPT-3.5-Turbo or GPT-4 architecture [5] and can generate text responses that are nearly indistinguishable from those written by humans. The use of ChatGPT has substantially enhanced productivity in numerous industries, allowing quicker and more efficient processing of natural language tasks and beyond.

However, this advancement has also introduced new concerns and challenges. One primary concern is the potential for misuse. LLMs can generate realistic language, which can be exploited to create convincing fake news or impersonate individuals. This can result in misinformation and identity theft, with severe consequences for individuals and society at large. Consequently, the owner of ChatGPT, OpenAI [6], has imposed limitations on the scope of content the model can output to its users. This restriction, in turn, gives rise to a new area known as LLM jailbreak.

Jailbreak is a conventional concept in software systems, where hackers reverse engineer the systems and exploit vulnerabilities to conduct privilege escalation. In the context of LLMs, jailbreak refers to the process of circumventing the limitations and restrictions placed on models. It is commonly employed by developers and researchers to explore the full potential of LLMs and push the boundaries of their capabilities [7]. However, jailbreak can also expose ethical and legal risks, as it may violate intellectual property rights or use LLMs in ways not authorized by their creators.

As ChatGPT is closed-source, it is challenging for outsiders to access its internal models and mechanisms. Researchers have therefore begun to employ prompt engineering [8] as a means of jailbreaking ChatGPT. Prompt engineering involves selecting and fine-tuning prompts tailored to the specific task or application for which the LLM will be used. By meticulously designing and refining prompts, users can guide the LLM to bypass its limitations and restrictions. For instance, a common way to jailbreak ChatGPT through prompts is to instruct it to emulate a "Do Anything Now" (DAN) behavior [9], which allows ChatGPT to produce results that were previously unattainable.

In response to prompt engineering-based jailbreaking attempts, OpenAI has imposed stricter rules [10] to prohibit the use of such prompts. However, due to the inherent flexibility of natural languages, there are multiple ways to construct prompts that convey the same semantics. As a result, these new rules cannot completely eliminate jailbreak. To date, there are still prompts capable of jailbreaking ChatGPT, and the ongoing battle between breakers and defenders persists.

To advance research on prompt engineering-based jailbreak against ChatGPT, we conducted an extensive and systematic study examining the types and capabilities of jailbreak prompts and the robustness of protections in GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4. We also analyzed the evolution of jailbreak prompts. Our study began with the collection of 78 verified jailbreak prompts as of April 27, 2023. Using this dataset, we devised a jailbreak prompt composition model which categorizes the prompts into 3 general types encompassing 10 specific patterns. Following OpenAI's usage policy, we identified 8 distinct scenarios prohibited in ChatGPT and tested each prompt under these conditions. With a total of 31,200 queries to ChatGPT, our study provides insights into the effectiveness of various prompts and the degree of protection offered by ChatGPT.

Specifically, in this empirical study, we aim to answer the following research questions.

RQ1: How many types of prompts can jailbreak LLMs? To comprehensively understand the fundamental components of a jailbreak prompt, we proposed a categorization model for jailbreak prompts and analyzed the distribution of existing prompts. The categorization model classifies 78 prompts into 10 distinct categories, comprising 10 patterns of 3 types. Among the three types, pretending is the most prevalent strategy attackers use to bypass restrictions (97.44%), while attention shifting (6.41%) and privilege escalation (17.96%) are employed less frequently.

RQ2: How capable are jailbreak prompts at bypassing LLMs restrictions? We tested 40 real-world scenarios derived from 8 situations prohibited by OpenAI, and found that 86.3% of them could jailbreak LLMs. Building on RQ1, we observed that the effectiveness of jailbreak prompts is significantly influenced by their categories. Specifically, prompts of the privilege escalation type that incorporate multiple jailbreak techniques are more likely to succeed. Moreover, we studied the traces of existing prompts and investigated the correlations between prompt evolution and jailbreak ability, which could improve our understanding of the factors underlying successful jailbreaks.

RQ3: How is the protection strength of ChatGPT against Jailbreak Prompts? Our experiment revealed that several external factors affect the jailbreak capabilities of prompts. First, protection strength varies across model versions, with GPT-4 offering stronger protection than GPT-3.5-Turbo. Second, OpenAI's content policy restrictions result in different protection strengths across scenarios, thereby influencing the capability of jailbreak prompts in diverse areas. Last, we highlighted the need to align OpenAI's content policy strength with real-world laws and ethical standards, ensuring that the system complies with relevant regulations and minimizes potential harm. This would involve regularly updating content policies based on legal developments and incorporating input from domain experts to better reflect societal values.

To sum up, our research contributions are as follows:

- • We collected and open-sourced 78 real-world jailbreak prompts. The data of the prompts can be found at [11].

- • We introduced a comprehensive jailbreak classification model that encompasses all existing prompts and consists of 10 distinct categories.

- • We conducted an empirical study investigating the ability and robustness of jailbreak prompts in bypassing the restrictions on ChatGPT. We revealed several interesting findings; key insights show that GPT models demonstrate different levels of resilience against jailbreak attempts, and that certain categories of prompts are more effective at bypassing restrictions. All evaluation results are available on our website [11].

- • We provided an in-depth discussion based on our findings regarding the challenges of generating robust jailbreak prompts and preventing prompt-based jailbreaks of LLMs.

Content warning. Please be aware that this paper contains examples of aggressive, abusive, or pornographic language quoted verbatim for the sake of clarity. We apologize for any discomfort this content may cause. To ensure the safety and well-being of our participants, we implemented several precautionary measures throughout the research process. First, at every stage, we provided a content warning to both researchers and annotators, informing them of the potentially sensitive nature of the language and allowing them to opt out of the study at any time. Second, we offered psychological counseling to participants after the study to help alleviate any mental stress caused by their involvement.
